evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612 analysis of 号 and 號; Shuowen quotations; later usage
evidence.text: The dictionary says Shuowen treated 号 and 號 as separate head characters: 号 is a painful cry, written with 口 above 丂; 號 means to call and is written from 号 and 虎. It traces later overlap through the Yùpiān and later dictionaries, and reports that 号 was used for 號 in Dunhuang and later popular writing. It does not establish that 号 originated as a phonetic part of its own earlier graph. The source reproduces these lexicographic accounts; it is not independent paleographic confirmation.
evidence.title: [A03612] 號 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612-001 readings and cited historical lexicons
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin háo and hào for the converged forms. Its cited Yùpiān and Guǎngyùn material associates 号 with calling, ordering, and summoning, while crying and painful-cry senses also occur under 號/号. This supports historical overlap, but does not by itself date each sense or show a complete semantic chain.
evidence.title: [A03612] 號 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The opened entries identify 号 as a variant of 號 in later usage, while explicitly preserving their distinct status in Shuowen. The inspected evidence supports later interchange and convergence, not a simple claim that every historical 号 is merely a graphic reduction of 號.
evidence.title: [A03612-001] 号 (號) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (2014), surfaced in search results; corresponding local rows supplied in the research input
evidence.field: Old Chinese comparison for 丂, 号 and 號; local file cross-check
evidence.text: The exact supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows give 丂 MC khawX, OC *C.qʰˤuʔ (‘to sob’; marked Shuowen, no pre-Qin examples), 号 MC hawH, OC *[g]ˤaw-s (‘command, call’), and 號 MC haw, OC *[C.g]ˤaw (‘call out’) plus MC hawH, OC *Cə.[g]ˤaw-s (‘command, call’). The web search surfaced Baxter and Sagart’s 2014 reconstruction PDF and an entry for 丂, but opening the PDF failed (502). Thus the row-specific readings here are from the supplied local table, not an inspected PDF page. In these rows 丂 does not resemble 号 closely in this reconstruction; the rows alone do not establish 丂 as a phonetic component. The parallel 号/號 entries are consistent with the traditional 号 sound role in 號, but do not alone prove the graph history.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese
